items.label: A cohesive spheroid
items.note: The clean case: one dense, roughly round cluster with a crisp edge. When frames look like this, every segmenter agrees and the shape numbers are trustworthy.

items.label: Fragmenting under drug
items.note: Under drug the cluster breaks into many pieces. Pixel overlap collapses and the outline becomes ambiguous, this is the hardest case and why CC-Dice is used.

items.label: Out of focus
items.note: A blurred frame: the boundary goes soft, so perimeter and roundness turn unreliable even when area is still recoverable.

items.label: Low contrast
items.note: The spheroid barely stands out from the field. A single global threshold cannot find this edge, which is why the production segmenter is learned, not a threshold.

items.label: Uneven illumination
items.note: Shading and debris across the field bias any intensity-based boundary, another reason the inversion leans on shape features, not raw pixels.

note: Real brightfield frames, the full field, normalised to their own intensity range as the pipeline does, with the AI outline in gold. Toggle it off for the frame alone. Metrics are the canonical frame-QC values.
